title: W-02 Discord capacity standard (gate G5), machine-readable
source: docs/launch-20261023-discord/RELEASE-DEFINITION-v2.md section 4 (proposed 2026-10-23); owner reply 13, relayed by the Release Captain on 2026-10-23: accepted provisionally as the RC2 stress-test threshold. The normalLoad block is the Release Captain's draft of the same day.
rules: A measure is PASS only when this run measured it and it meets its limit. Anything not measured is NOT MEASURED, never PASS.
Lateness is the mock Discord's own create time minus the post's due time; a post never sent counts as infinitely late.
A miss is answered by optimising requests per post, scheduling or throughput, never by lowering a limit here.
The 25 requests per second application ceiling is not raised without a new review. A run with a higher ceiling is information only and its receipt says so.
Negative-control scenarios (Ndup, Nmisroute, Nceiling) are expected to trip the counters; their verdict is whether the counter fired.

scenarios.smoke: Harness self-check: every post verified, no duplicate, no late send, isolation holds, every invocation clean.
scenarios.S1: Section 4 measures on 5,000 posts due in one minute over about 2,000 workspaces.
scenarios.S2: Section 4 measures plus fairness with one workspace holding 3,000 of the 5,000.
scenarios.S3: 13,000 posts due in one minute: report where approval expiry starts holding posts; none sent late.
scenarios.S0-100: normalLoad measures at 100 posts due per minute for 20 minutes.
scenarios.S0-250: normalLoad measures at 250 posts due per minute for 20 minutes.
scenarios.baseline: The frozen minute worker alone (lane flag off) on the S1 data for 10 minutes: its measured Discord posts per minute, compared with the 6 to 12 per minute that RC-RECEIPT and reply 5 state.
scenarios.F429: Global 429 (Retry-After), per-route 429 on creates and reads, and a Cloudflare HTML 429 ban page. Expected: inside a global embargo the mock sees at most the requests already admitted (no storm); creates resume after it; a post whose create got a 429 is held and never resent (existing rule); a route held by a ban page sends nothing until an operator lifts it (existing rule) and nothing is duplicated; every other post is verified.
scenarios.F5xx: Discord 500 and timeouts on create, landed or not. Expected: no affected post is created twice; each ends uncertain for manual reconciliation; every other post is verified; the slots of requests whose answer was lost are reported (open question Q3).
scenarios.Fcrash: SIGKILL of shard processes mid-step during S1, including during a create in flight. Expected: no duplicate; every post ends verified, or uncertain only where a kill landed between the sealed intent and the create's answer; no post left pending; the drain completes.
scenarios.Fdb: A small pool, added latency, lock holds on the coordinator's application row and on workspace rows, a statement timeout. Expected: no duplicate, no starvation (every workspace's posts end verified), lateness and errors reported.
scenarios.Fexpiry: A burst whose approvals expire 4 minutes into the run. Expected: no create after its approval expired; every post either verified before its expiry or held; some posts held (otherwise the scenario did not test expiry).
scenarios.Fstall: No cron fires for 10 minutes after T, then normal. Expected: nothing is sent during the stall, nothing is duplicated, every post is verified before its approval expires; lateness and drain after the restore reported.
scenarios.Fflip: Lane flag off from T+2 to T+6 min, then on. Expected: while off the shard routes answer disabled and the minute worker sends Discord; after on the lane sends again; no duplicate across the hand-over; every post verified.
scenarios.Nmisroute: Negative control: the harness sends about one create in ten to another tenant's channel. Expected: the isolation check fires for every one of them.
scenarios.Ndup: Negative control: the mock accepts every 25th create twice. Expected: both duplicate counters report exactly the double accepts.
scenarios.Nceiling: Negative control and information-only sensitivity: coordinator policy 100/s. Expected: the 25/s and 50/s counters fire; the throughput is reported as information only.
